site.title: Mushrooms of the Delaware Water Gap and Sourlands
site.tagline: A living field gallery — grouped by genus, mapped by GPS across NJ, PA, and MA.
site.disclaimer: This site is for education and appreciation only. It is not a foraging guide. Never eat a wild mushroom unless an expert has confirmed the identification.

groups.edibility: Many toxic or deadly — treat all as poisonous unless expertly identified
groups.summary: Mycorrhizal gilled mushrooms including yellow patches, warty Lepidella types, pale striate grisettes, white buttons, and brown-warted blushers. Free white gills and a volva are classic clues.
groups.uses: Not for the table unless expertly identified. Many Amanita species are deadly.
groups.field_marks: Free white gills; often ring and/or volva; white spore print.

groups.edibility: Variable by species — never eat without confident ID
groups.summary: Pored mushrooms of oak woods: two-colored boletes, brown boletes, orange-capped types, and pale boletes.
groups.uses: Variable; only eat after confident ID and thorough cooking. Avoid red-pored unknowns.
groups.habitat: Soil in oak and mixed woods after rain; mycorrhizal.
groups.tree_associates: Oaks and mixed hardwoods of the Sourlands.
groups.field_marks: Pores under the cap; thick stems; fleshy caps.
groups.region_notes: Abundant in Sourland oak woods. Also Middlesex Fells (MA).

id_detail.scientific_name: Boletus cf. auripes / yellow bolete complex
id_detail.edibility: Many yellow-pored boletes are edible when well ID'd; confirm species — educational only here
id_detail.summary: Pair of boletes with orange-tan caps, bright yellow stems, and yellow sponge-like pores. Growing in pine needles and oak litter under mixed woods. Matches the butter-foot / yellow bolete look (Boletus auripes and allies).
id_detail.uses: Some related yellow boletes are choice edibles when correctly identified and cooked; always rule out bitter and blue-staining toxic lookalikes. Not a foraging recommendation.
id_detail.habitat: Mycorrhizal on forest floor under hardwoods and mixed stands.
id_detail.tree_associates: Oaks and mixed hardwoods; pine needles often present in mixed stands.
id_detail.field_marks: Orange-tan to yellow-brown dry cap; yellow pore surface (tubes); thick bright yellow stem; no gills.
id_detail.photo_location: Middlesex Fells Reservation, Stoneham / Medford, MA
id_detail.season: Summer to fall (this find: early August)

groups.region_notes: Common in Sourland oak woods; also Middlesex Fells (MA).

id_detail.edibility: Do not eat — many acrid or GI-upsetting; needs species-level ID
id_detail.summary: Bright pink-red to rose cap with pure white gills and a white stem. Brittle flesh typical of Russula. Growing on moss among pine needles in mixed woods — often compared to the emetica / silvicola complex; taste (mild vs peppery) and peel would refine species.
id_detail.uses: Not for the table without expert species ID. Many red Russulas are acrid or cause stomach upset.
id_detail.habitat: Mycorrhizal on forest floor; mossy spots under pine and mixed hardwoods.
id_detail.tree_associates: Pine and mixed hardwoods (oak/beech common regionally).
id_detail.field_marks: Pink-red smooth cap (often depressed in center); pure white close gills; white stem without ring or volva; brittle chalky flesh.
id_detail.photo_location: Middlesex Fells Reservation, Stoneham / Medford, MA
id_detail.season: Summer to fall (this find: early August)

groups.field_marks: Tan-brown wavy cap; brown gills; thick stem; inrolled margin when young.

id_detail.edibility: Toxic — can cause serious immune-mediated poisoning; do not eat
id_detail.summary: Large tan-to-brown gilled mushroom with a wavy, often inrolled margin and brown gills. Young button nearby. In oak and mixed litter. Formerly eaten in parts of Europe; now known to be dangerously toxic.
id_detail.uses: Not edible. Documented severe reactions after repeated consumption. Educational only.
id_detail.habitat: Mycorrhizal under conifers and hardwoods; leaf litter and mossy soil.
id_detail.tree_associates: Pine, birch, oak, and mixed woods.
id_detail.field_marks: Tan-brown cap with lobed/wavy margin; brown close gills that may bruise darker; thick stem; often clustered with buttons; margin inrolled when young.
id_detail.photo_location: Middlesex Fells Reservation, Stoneham / Medford, MA
id_detail.season: Summer to fall (this find: early August)
